subsystems.name: Cell source and expansion
subsystems.role: supplies the patient's own cells so the implant is not rejected.
parts: induced pluripotent or adult stem cell culture

subsystems.name: Bio-ink
subsystems.role: the printable carrier that holds living cells and keeps them alive during and after printing.
parts: hydrogel base such as alginate, gelatin or collagen

subsystems.name: Bioprinter and print strategy
subsystems.role: places different cell types and structural materials in the right three-dimensional positions.
parts: extrusion, inkjet or laser-assisted print heads
multiple print heads for several inks
support bath or sacrificial scaffold for overhangs
imaging-derived digital model of the organ

subsystems.name: Structural scaffold
subsystems.role: gives the soft printed tissue a shape it can hold while it matures.

subsystems.name: Vascular network
subsystems.role: puts blood vessels through the tissue so cells beyond a fraction of a millimetre from a capillary do not die.
parts: printed channels and branching vessel trees
perfusion connections to the host circulation

subsystems.name: Bioreactor and maturation
subsystems.role: conditions the printed construct until it behaves like organ tissue.
parts: sensors for oxygen, pH and pressure

subsystems.name: Quality control and regulatory testing
subsystems.role: proves the construct is sterile, functional and safe before implantation.

buildSteps.title: Take a biopsy
buildSteps.detail: A small sample of the patient's tissue is taken and its cells separated in the lab.

buildSteps.title: Expand and reprogram the cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells are grown to large numbers, and reprogrammed or directed to become the several cell types the organ needs — working tissue cells, vessel-lining cells and support cells.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the bio-ink
buildSteps.detail: Cells are mixed into a hydrogel that flows through a print nozzle but sets into a soft solid, with a density and viscosity tuned so the cells survive printing.

buildSteps.title: Design the organ
buildSteps.detail: Scans such as CT or MRI are converted into a digital model showing the shape of the organ and the branching paths of its vessels.

buildSteps.title: Print the construct
buildSteps.detail: The printer lays down structural ink, cell-laden inks and a sacrificial ink that will later be washed out to leave channels, layer by layer over hours.

buildSteps.title: Remove the sacrificial ink and line the vessels
buildSteps.detail: The temporary channel ink is dissolved away and the empty channels are seeded with vessel-lining cells, or blood is perfused through them.

buildSteps.title: Mature in a bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: The construct is kept perfused and, for muscle-type organs, stretched or electrically paced for days to weeks so the cells organise and the scaffold degrades.

buildSteps.title: Test and implant
buildSteps.detail: Tissue checks, sterility testing and animal studies precede surgical implantation, where the organ's vessels are joined to the patient's blood supply.

prerequisites.why: turning stem cells into the exact mix of organ cell types, at scale and without tumour risk, is not yet routine.
materials that print accurately and then support cells long enough for the tissue to mature are still being developed.
cells more than a fraction of a millimetre from a blood supply die, so a full-size solid organ needs a complete printed vessel network.

prerequisites.tech: Perfusion bioreactors that scale to whole organs
prerequisites.why: keeping a large construct fed and sterile for weeks is demonstrated only for small tissues.

prerequisites.tech: A regulatory route for living implants
prerequisites.why: regulators have no settled framework for approving a printed organ made from a patient's own cells.

pathway.milestone: printed thin and hollow tissues — skin, cornea, cartilage, bladder patches — plus organ-on-chip models for drug testing
pathway.unlocks: real clinical use in simple repairs and a faster, animal-free way to test medicines.

pathway.milestone: tubular and hollow organs such as blood vessels and airways reach clinical trials
pathway.unlocks: proof that printed constructs survive and function in patients.

pathway.milestone: organ patches and assist devices — cardiac patches, kidney tissue implants — used alongside existing treatments
pathway.unlocks: partial restoration of organ function for people on transplant waiting lists.

pathway.milestone: whole solid organs with printed vessel trees, matured in bioreactors
pathway.unlocks: on-demand, rejection-free replacement of kidneys, livers and hearts — the point at which donor waiting lists could end.
